## Research Overview

My research focuses on political economy, labor policy, and global health. I use applied econometric methods and large-scale survey and administrative data to examine how institutions and public policies shape demographic, labor market, and health outcomes.

## Ongoing Projects

### Loss and Longing: Child Loss and Fertility Intentions in Bangladesh

This project examines how experiencing child loss shapes fertility intentions using nationally representative Bangladesh DHS data. I analyze how demographic, socioeconomic, and household factors interact with reproductive preferences after loss. The study contributes to demographic research and reproductive health policy discussions.  
(PAA 2026 – Poster Presentation)

---


### Wrongful Discharge Laws and Labor Productivity

This project studies how the adoption of wrongful discharge laws affects labor productivity and firm outcomes. Leveraging state-level policy variation, I use quasi-experimental methods to assess dynamic effects over time. The research contributes to the political economy of labor regulation and institutional design.  
(MPSA 2026 – Working Paper Series)



### Employer-Sponsored Childcare and Employee Retention

This project evaluates whether employer-sponsored childcare programs improve employee retention. Using quasi-experimental strategies, including regression discontinuity designs, I analyze how access to childcare affects workforce stability. The study informs work-family policy and employer-level labor strategies.  
(WSSA 2026 – Poster Presentation)

---


### PEPFAR Funding and Antiretroviral Drug Prices

This project investigates the relationship between PEPFAR funding flows and antiretroviral drug price trends over time. Using cross-national time-series data, I examine whether large-scale donor financing influences market affordability and treatment access. The project contributes to debates on global health financing and procurement sustainability.

---

## Methods

My work applies difference-in-differences, event-study models, regression discontinuity designs, and panel data methods. I primarily use R and Stata for reproducible research and policy-oriented analysis.
